text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — weird batching incident around 2026-03-15T15:12 UTC. batch_utilization jumped to ~94% but tokens/sec for g4-pool-3 dropped ~28% and queue depth climbed.

Maya Patel: I saw the spike on Grafana. kv_cache_hit_rate fell from ~0.88 -> ~0.61 at ~15:14 UTC. avg_tokens_per_batch decreased ~18% while batch slot fill (by count) increased.

Tony Rivera: Starting perf capture on g4-pool-3. Hypothesis: kernel-selector falling back to a slower kernel for short sequences when cache misses rise; per-token overhead increases.

Priya Sinha: That time overlaps the kernel-selector rollout. I'll pull canary logs and queue_events to correlate deploy time with cache misses.

Alex Chen: Dashboards lacked a couple of quick-debug panels. Can we add kv_cache_hit_rate, token_sec_per_instance, microbatch_count, queue_depth p50/p90/p99, head_of_line_latency, selected_kernel distribution, and a heatmap for batch_tokens vs latency?

Maya Patel: Yep. Will add those panels and an annotation lane for deploys. Also creating alert: kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.7 AND avg_tokens_per_batch < 8 for >2m => page runtime-oncall.

Tony Rivera: PromQL drafts:
- tokens/sec per instance: sum by(instance)(rate(tokens_processed_total[1m]))
- kv cache hit rate: increase(sum(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / increase(sum(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))
- selected kernel counts: count by (kernel)(selected_kernel_total)

Maya Patel: Adding a derived `batch_token_utilization = sum(tokens_in_batches) / sum(max_tokens_capacity)` to catch "full" batches that are low on tokens.

Priya Sinha: queue_events already contains request_id + cache_status. I can join to Jaeger traces for 15:0815:30 UTC and surface top slow traces where cache_status=miss.

InfraBot: deploy: kernel-selector/v1.9.1 promoted to g4-pool-3 at 2026-03-15T15:12:03Z :rocket:

Tony Rivera: Captured flamegraphs. Attention kernel time increased ~2.3x for seq_len < 32 when selector chose `generic_attn_v0`. That explains lower tokens/sec even though batch slots were filled.

Alex Chen: So pattern: cache miss -> smaller effective request tokens -> selector chooses fallback generic kernel -> per-token throughput drops -> backlog grows even though batch_utilization (by slot count) is high.

Maya Patel: Dashboard plan: Overview row with global token/sec, avg_tokens_per_batch, batch_token_utilization, kv_cache_hit_rate; plus drilldowns: per-instance tokens/sec, kernel distribution pie, batch_size vs latency heatmap, and queue depth percentiles. Will annotate deploy times.

Tony Rivera: Tactical proposals:
1) Avoid generic fallback for seq_len < 64 unless kernel failure flagged.
2) Introduce a cache-aware kernel preference: if kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.75, prefer kernels optimized for miss-heavy workloads.
3) Bias batching policy to increase token budget target when cache hit drops (if latency SLO allows waiting an extra X ms).

Priya Sinha: Running trace join now. I will post top-10 request_ids with selected_kernel and cache_status and attach CSV of seq_len bucket vs avg latency.

Maya Patel: ETA for dashboard + alerts = EOD. Adding heatmap panel and a compact widget for selected_kernel counts per model.

Tony Rivera: Scheduling A/B: 30m baseline, 30m with selector heuristic change on a small canary. Will compare tokens/sec and latency buckets (p50/p95).

Alex Chen: Ops action list:
- Maya: push dashboard + alert rule + deploy annotations
- Tony: run A/B and post perf numbers + flamegraphs
- Priya: post trace-join CSV and top-k slow traces
- Platform: consider a circuit-breaker to pin short sequences to stable kernel until selector stabilizes

Maya Patel: Also adding an alert for `batch_token_utilization < 0.5 while batch_utilization > 0.8` (indicates many small-token requests filling slots).

Priya Sinha: Trace join results (preliminary): majority of top slow traces had cache_status=miss and selected_kernel=generic_attn_v0. CSV attaching in next message.

InfraBot: note: autoscaler flapped 1 instance at 2026-03-15T15:17:10Z due to ephemeral OOM during the spike.

Tony Rivera: If A/B shows improvement, we'll backport a micro-optimization into `generic_attn_v0` to reduce per-call overhead for short sequences.

Alex Chen: Long-term requests: (1) emit selected_kernel{name,version} metric, (2) surface batch_token_utilization in the runtime SLO dashboard, (3) integrate cache-aware batching policy that raises token budget target when cache hit drops.

Maya Patel: Dashboard draft link (internal): https://grafana.redwood/d/xyz987/batching-telemetry (will paste panel JSON once stable).

Tony Rivera: Posting flamegraph SVGs and a short results table after the A/B. Will include columns: config, seq_len_bucket, tokens/sec, latency_p50, latency_p95.

Priya Sinha: Trace CSV and top-10 slow traces posted in follow-up. Many examples show repeated short-attn runs with cache misses and generic kernel.

Alex Chen: Thanks team. Let's validate selector change in staging, roll slowly, and keep dashboards/alerts in place so oncall can detect recurrence quickly. :thumbsup:
